My land is 72 mu. I've been working it for 25 years. Cotton is what I know — it's what this county grows, it's what I've always done. Sunflower I keep on a portion because the market has been decent and it doesn't need as much attention during the busy cotton season, which helps since my wife and I are managing most of this ourselves with the kids working in the city.

Cotton will get the bulk of the land — 50 mu. I switched to Bt hybrid seeds several years back. They cost more but I spray less for bollworm. Still have to spray for aphids and mites and other things, so I'll do about 5 applications. I'll rotary till in spring before planting. For fertilizer I follow what I've learned over the years — about 16 kg nitrogen per mu, split between base and topdressing. Phosphorus around 9, potassium around 11. I'll irrigate 4 times: at establishment, budding, peak flowering, and when bolls are setting. My well covers all of this. I expect around 280 kg seed cotton per mu — last few years have been close to that.

The other 22 mu goes to sunflower. I plant it in summer. Improved seeds, not hybrid — cheaper, and sunflower doesn't vary as much in this area. Much lighter on inputs. Two or three irrigations, two pesticide sprays mainly for moth. I rotary till here too. Yield around 180 kg per mu is what I count on.

With only the two of us and the cotton harvest being so labor-intensive in autumn, I can't take on more. This balance works.
